concepts.def: Queen of England 1558-1603, last Tudor monarch
Elizabeth's traveling household of around 1,000 people
Earl of Leicester and Elizabeth's lifelong favourite
Royal gifts and jobs Elizabeth used to control nobles
Royal tour of nobles' houses, showing off the queen

walkthroughs.body_html:
The royal court had around 1,000 people.

It travelled between palaces like Whitehall, Greenwich and Hampton Court. Courtiers competed for the queen's attention — and the patronage she could give. Style, dance and witty talk mattered hugely.

Robert Dudley, Earl of Leicester, was Elizabeth's lifelong favourite — possibly even her love.

Later came Robert Devereux, Earl of Essex. He grew arrogant, led a failed rebellion in 1601 and was executed. Elizabeth was said to mourn him deeply.

Elizabeth ruled with her Privy Council, Parliament and JPs.

Each summer she went on 'progress' — visiting nobles' houses to be seen by her people. It saved money and let her show off her power. Hosting Elizabeth was costly but a great honour.
